Question: How does a dominant wolf choose its mate when it has multiple options? Is there a clear hierarchy between the alpha male/female and the other wolves?
Answer: The same way you choose yours - whichever of those options he or she likes best. There’s no set criteria for that. The other wolves in a pack are the mated pair’s children, so yes, the kids are expected to listen to mom and dad.

Question: What other birds are considered to be very intelligent, besides crows, owls and parrots?
Answer: That’s an interesting question, because you used the words ‘considered to be,’ and included owls. So I can only guess that you mean ‘considered to be’ by laypersons - common people, not scientists. Scientists certainly do not consider owls to be very intelligent. They are objectively rather unintelligent birds. (Frankly, birds as a group are very smart animals - generally smarter than mammals - but comparing one bird to another, owls aren’t that bright). Other birds considered to be intelligent by lay persons, include Australian magpies, all corvid birds (not just crows, but also ravens, magpies, jackdaws, jays, etc), seagulls, red-crowned cranes (which can transform into humans in folklore), and Tui birds. Some of these are truly very intelligent birds, and others are less so.

Question: Is there a relationship between dinosaurs and birds? Could this potentially lead to the resurrection of extinct dinosaur species in the future?
Answer: It’s the same as the relationship between mammals and humans. Birds are dinosaurs. No, we won’t be resurrecting any extinct dinosaur species. The reason we won’t be doing that is that the DNA that made them unique species has been lost. It doesn’t exist any longer. And while we might get the occasional snippet of protein from fossils, DNA is fragile, and we will never be able to find enough to restore even a single complete gene from a non-avian dinosaur species. Their genomes are gone forever. What we could potentially do is use genetic engineering to create something similar using bird DNA as a base. But that, too, is a long way off. Cloning and genetically engineering animal that reproduce via amniote eggs isn’t something we’ve managed to solve yet, just for starters. Because of the way eggs form, it’s a horrifically difficult problem. With placental mammals, you can just inject some hormones and pop the embryo into the uterus, and a lot of times it will embed and grow. But the embyro of an egg-laying animal has to actually be embedded at the exact right stage of development while the egg is forming! You can’t take an infertile egg and put an embryo in it, it doesn’t work. So far, we’ve been able to create only the simplest organism using a printed DNA genome and a cell that has been emptied of its DNA. So it’s going to be a long while before we understand DNA and the proteome well enough to create a complex life form, much less tailor one to look and behave the way we want it to.

Question: Are there any animals alive today that are classified as dinosaurs? If so, what are they called and how do we know this for sure?
Answer: Yes. The only dinosaurs to survive the K-Pg extinction were in the clade Aves. We call them birds. :) We know this for certain because we have found the fossil evidence showing the evolution of birds. The incredible find of detailed feather fossils associated with non-avian dinosaurs in China clinched it. Birds are dinosaurs, not just descendants of dinosaurs. Birds are not all that distinct from other small theropods.

Question: What is the largest known dinosaur? Are there any larger dinosaurs that we are aware of? Were there any flying dinosaurs larger than Quetzalcoatlus?
Answer: What is the largest known dinosaur? Argentinosaurus huinculensis is probably the largest dinosaur known at this time. Are there any larger dinosaurs that we are aware of? If there were, wouldn’t that one be the largest dinosaur known? Were there any flying dinosaurs larger than Quetzalcoatlus? No. Quetzalcoatlus is a genus of pterosaurs (not dinosaurs). No flying dinosaur has ever become as large as the biggest pterosaurs. Flying dinosaurs were represented in several clades, but the best known is Avialae - the birds. (Birds are flying dinosaurs). The largest flying dinosaur known was a bird named Argentavis magnificens. Its wingspan was in the range of 5.09 to 6.5 m (16 ft 8 in to 21 ft 4 in). The bird probably weighed 70 to 72 kg (154 to 159 lb). So quite a bit smaller than Quetzalcoatlus. Quetzalcoatlus northropi had a wingspan of around 10 m (33 ft). Its estimated weight was 200–250 kg (440–550 lb). A truly huge animal.
